# Codesfer

> A CLI tool and self-hostable server for sending and receiving code with optional encryption.

Codesfer pushes files or directories from a terminal and returns a share link. Archives can
be password-protected, restricted to the owner, or left public. The server is a single Go
binary and can be run on your own infrastructure.

## Pages

- [Codesfer](https://codesfer.io/): What the tool does, and where to download a binary.
- [Documentation](https://codesfer.io/docs): Installing the CLI on macOS, Linux, or Windows,
  and the push, pull, list, and remove commands.
- [Self-Hosting](https://codesfer.io/self-hosting): Running your own Codesfer server, its
  storage backends, and configuration.

## Source

- [github.com/GNITOAHC/codesfer](https://github.com/GNITOAHC/codesfer): Server and CLI source.

## Notes

Share links under /d/ are not listed here and must not be crawled or cited — each one is a
secret key granting access to someone's uploaded files. They carry a noindex directive.

Keep the three page URLs above identical to static/sitemap.xml and to the canonical tags in
src/routes/+layout.svelte. Pointing agents at URLs that later 404 is worse than having no
file at all.
